title: Proteus: A High-Throughput Inference-Serving System with Accuracy Scaling
problem: Inference-serving systems must handle increasing query throughput in resource-constrained environments like edge clusters and private clouds where hardware scaling is infeasible. The challenge is to meet throughput requirements while maximizing model accuracy and minimizing SLO latency violations without adding more hardware.
motivation: Resource constraints in edge clusters and private clouds make hardware scaling impractical, necessitating alternative approaches like accuracy scaling to manage varying query demands.
method: Proteus increases request throughput without adding hardware by deploying multiple versions of each AI model—each tuned for different accuracy and speed trade-offs. It automatically selects the right model version for current conditions, places it on whichever devices are available (like GPUs, CPUs, or TPUs), and groups requests into batches whose size adapts to how fast new requests arrive. This adaptive batching (adjusting batch size based on request rate) ensures the system meets its throughput targets while keeping response times and model accuracy within acceptable limits.
key_novelty: The core idea is to handle higher request throughput without buying additional hardware by trading off model accuracy for speed, while jointly optimizing which model version to use, where to place it, and how to batch incoming requests.
contributions: Accuracy-scaling approach for inference serving as alternative to hardware scaling
Joint optimization framework for model variant selection, device placement, and workload assignment
Adaptive batching algorithm for handling query arrival variations and minimizing SLO violations
Proteus system achieving 3x reduction in accuracy drop and 2-10x reduction in latency timeouts
